newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mostly lower, trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mostly lower, trade quiet.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures ended lower in quiet trade, under pressure from strong U.S. consumer confidence data and firm U.S. asset prices.
Traders said stable Treasury bonds and a rally in U.S. stocks after losses Monday lent a firm tone to the dollar and kept key currencies near session lows most of the day.

U.S. June consumer confidence was a factor in the sound dollar tone. The Conference Board reported its confidence index at 129.6, the highest since August 1969. The forecast had been for a 126.3 reading.
Traders said they now await Japan's tankan report.
The Bank of Japan's quarterly survey of corporate sentiment was seen as an important key to the BOJ's monetary policy and would be widely watched as a clue to the Japanese economy, traders said.

"We've got the tankan tonight, and basically the consensus is for a flat report," one IMM currency analyst said. "If it's positive at all at this point it'll be bearish for the dollar," he said. The report is due at 1950 EDT/2350 GMT.
The dollar was firm all session, overcoming overnight worries that Japan might be tempted to sell U.S. Treasuries for gold.

Japanese Prime Minister Hashimoto's answer to a question Monday afternoon raised that concern, weighing on dollar/yen and U.S. stocks late Monday and overnight. Later, however, Japan's Finance Ministry said Hashimoto's remarks had been misunderstood, and the dollar returned to positive ground.
By Tuesday afternoon, most currencies languished near the bottom of the day's range.
Traders said action was thin, and noted no reaction to an as-expected Treasury two-year note auction or to the latest Redbook retail sales index, which rose 1.6 percent.
"They stayed in the ranges and the dollar stayed on the bid side," a currency futures trader said.
Another trader said mark/yen cross activity would likely remain the focus and reflect reaction to the tankan report.
"People are expecting a pretty poor report and that's what people are looking to," he said.

At the close, September yen was up $0.000004 to $0.008805, marks fell $0.0021 to $0.5831, Swiss francs fell $0.0042 to $0.7011, sterling fell $0.0058 to $1.6624, Canadian dollars fell $0.0019 to $0.7228 and Mexican pesos were $0.000150 higher at $0.121600.
